fields.title: MAN ME B/C
fields.description:
Electronic propulsion has become the industry standard across modern merchant fleets, requiring marine engineers to possess a deep understanding of intelligent engine management systems. This course provides practical training in the operation, monitoring, diagnostics, and maintenance of MAN B&W ME electronically controlled engines.

What You Will Learn:
- Principles of MAN B&W ME electronic engine technology
- Engine control architecture and automation systems
- Safe operation and monitoring procedures
- Alarm interpretation and fault diagnostics
- Preventive maintenance and troubleshooting techniques
- Best engineering practices for modern electronically controlled propulsion

Why This Course Matters:
Modern shipping companies increasingly operate electronically controlled propulsion plants, making practical ME engine knowledge one of the most valuable competencies for marine engineers.

Career Value:
After completing this course, you will strengthen your technical competence, improve your readiness for modern ME-powered vessels, and increase your professional value within the international maritime industry.

fields.title: Twin Engine & Steering Gear
fields.description:
Reliable propulsion and steering systems are fundamental to the safe operation of every vessel. This course provides a practical understanding of twin-engine propulsion arrangements and steering gear systems, covering their design, operation, maintenance, inspection, and emergency procedures.

What You Will Learn:
- Twin-engine propulsion principles
- Steering gear construction and operation
- Hydraulic and control system fundamentals
- Emergency steering procedures
- Inspection and preventive maintenance
- Common failures and troubleshooting methods

Why This Course Matters:
Failures involving propulsion or steering remain among the most critical technical incidents at sea.

Career Value:
Develop practical engineering competence that supports safe vessel operation and enhances your ability to maintain critical propulsion and steering systems.

What You Will Learn:
- LPG cargo handling operations
- Cargo planning fundamentals
- Ballast management procedures
- Cargo system configuration
- Operational safety during transfer
- International best practices for LPG operations

Why This Course Matters:
Efficient cargo operations directly influence vessel safety, commercial performance, and environmental protection.

Career Value:
Gain practical operational knowledge required to safely conduct cargo and ballast operations onboard modern LPG carriers while strengthening your professional competence within the gas shipping sector.

Build practical bridge management skills and strengthen your readiness to operate modern electronic navigation systems across the global merchant fleet.

fields.title: Tank Inspection
fields.description:
Develop the practical knowledge required to perform safe and effective inspections of cargo tanks onboard oil, chemical and gas carriers. This course explains inspection planning, safety precautions, structural assessment, coating evaluation, defect identification, reporting procedures and compliance with international maritime regulations.

What You Will Learn:
- Tank entry preparation
- Risk assessment procedures
- Gas measurement and atmosphere testing
- Structural inspection techniques
- Coating condition assessment
- Corrosion identification
- Crack and deformation detection
- Inspection reporting standards
- IACS and Class requirements
- Best industry practices

Why This Course Matters:
Proper tank inspections directly influence vessel safety, cargo integrity and classification compliance.

Career Value:
Improve inspection competence, increase technical knowledge, enhance safety awareness, reduce operational risks, strengthen professional credibility, advance your tanker career.
